text:
Ranking stability alone cannot establish missing-input robustness: a history-insensitive popularity predictor can remain perfectly stable. Missing-input research distinguishes ranking accuracy from ranking stability ([Amazon Science](https://assets.amazon.science/ea/6b/d2f305e64d1394abe7839be6e976/robust-training-of-sequential-recommender-systems-with-missing-input-data.pdf)); sequence-analysis work also shows SASRec can tolerate history shuffling ([dataset analysis](https://ceur-ws.org/Vol-2955/paper8.pdf)). Recommended controlled audit: compare baseline and masking-trained SASRec on identical validation users, targets and candidates, reporting absolute clean and corrupted HR@10/NDCG@10, paired changes and user-bootstrap intervals across predefined corruption levels. Smaller degradation is insufficient if clean accuracy already collapsed. Repeat corruption draws with shared seeds across models.

Match the number of removed nonpadding interactions when comparing recent versus older masking; include random masking and separately test last-item removal. Keep targets unchanged, specify whether positions are preserved or sequences compacted, and prevent padding or final-feature extraction artifacts. Stratify results within each category by original usable history length and target-item popularity computed exclusively from training interactions; report group sizes and uncertainty. Compare against training-frequency popularity, last-item-only, shuffled-order and length/popularity-matched swapped-history controls. Measure target-rank changes alongside top-10 overlap, recommendation popularity and cross-user similarity. These are proposed controls: useful contextual robustness should preserve ranking quality while still responding to meaningful history changes; shuffling alone tests order sensitivity.

Freeze each user’s candidate set and original-history exclusion policy across corruptions. Sampled rankings can disagree with full-catalog rankings ([Krichene–Rendle](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/)). Preserve selection exactly: four-category macro validation HR@10, 200 users/category, 99 unique negatives, evaluation seed 42. Keep corruption, popularity-matched-candidate and full-catalog audits auxiliary; never substitute them for selection or access hidden test labels.
